editorial:
Imagine you are watching a gritty look at city life where one bad encounter changes everything. You meet Carol, a kind welfare worker who just wants to help people, and George Lease, a pool attendant who is hiding a lot of anger. The movie starts off slow, but things get tense quickly when George attacks Carol in a public swimming pool. It feels like a raw, old-school TV drama that focuses more on the messy parts of human nature than on big explosions or flashy effects. You will feel the tension grow as the story explores why George did it and how Carol tries to deal with the trauma.

The acting is really solid, and you can tell the actors care about their roles. The pacing is a bit slow in the middle, but the psychological side of the story keeps you interested. If you like dramas that feel real and a bit uncomfortable, you will love this. Since it is an older title, you might have to hunt it down.
endingExplained: At the end, the movie focuses on the fallout of the attack and the legal battle that follows. You see George face the consequences of his actions, but the story does not give you a perfectly happy ending. It wraps up by showing that while the law can punish a criminal, the emotional scars for Carol take much longer to heal. The final scenes leave you thinking about how city life can isolate people until they snap.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school character studies and intense dramas.
